display_name: Record an accepted authorization that has not fired yet
description: Accepted-authorization obligations (wgr_d854aa6c). Records one authorization a seat ACCEPTED whose act waits on an external precondition — for example a standing seed-clone authorization that fires only once a clone URL and sealed sha are published. The accepting seat (usually the owed_by_role holder, such as Git-Controller) calls this at acceptance time: nothing ingests messages automatically, so an acceptance that is never recorded stays invisible to a successor. The entry starts in state accepted at version 1 with an immutable record event, both written in one transaction, and list_held_authorizations reports it beside open refusals with entry_kind accepted. A reissue that moves the predicate is a correction (change_accepted_authorization), not a new record. Bookkeeping only: recording performs no act, and the entry is an obligation index — never proof that the authorization is valid and never landing permission, which only the register's landing-authorization receipt gives. Open to any caller like the refusal-queue verbs: actor is reported provenance, not a grant.
embedding_description: Writing down a standing authorization that was accepted but has not fired yet because it waits on a precondition, such as a seed clone that fires once a URL and sealed sha are published. Stores who owes the act, the authorizing message, the act and its exact predicate so a fresh successor sees the open obligation.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: {"entry_id": "aau_...", "status": "recorded", "state": "accepted", "version": 1, "event_id": "aae_...", "entry": {projection snapshot}} — entry_id and version are what the next change_accepted_authorization call needs.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Name the act that is owed, who owes it and the predicate it waits on. Never describe the entry as authority to act or to land; it records an obligation.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: One typed state transaction inserting the accepted_authorization row and its record event. No caller-identity check — the record-at-acceptance convention is documented, not enforced.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: missing_argument: one of requesting_peer, owed_by_role, branch_or_request_ref, authorizing_message_id, act, predicate, reason or actor was empty. invalid_argument: notes was supplied blank. state_service_unavailable: the state service is not bound.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: Fix argument errors and resend. Not safe to blind-retry after a fault of unknown outcome: a retry after a write that actually landed records a second entry, so read back with get_authorization_history by authorizing_message_id (or list_held_authorizations) first. This verb is never retried automatically.
